Question 1

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points A(2,−5,1), P(4,−2,3) and Q(5,1,0).

a
15x−8y−3z+70=0
b
15x−8y−3z−67=0
c
2x−5y+z−70=0
d
4x−2y+3z=0
e
5x+y−67=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The vectors AP=(2,3,2) and AQ=(3,6,-1) have cross product (-15,8,3), so (15,-8,-3) is normal to the plane. Using A gives 15(x-2)-8(y+5)-3(z-1)=0, which simplifies to 15x-8y-3z-67=0.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(2,-5,1)$, $P(4,-2,3)$ and $Q(5,1,0).$
after.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨2,-5,1⟩,\,p=⟨4,-2,3⟩,$ and $q=⟨5,1,0⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨4,-2,3⟩-⟨2,-5,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,3,2⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨5,1,0⟩-⟨2,-5,1⟩ \\  & =⟨3,6,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-15i+8j+3k \\  & =⟨-15,8,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-15,8,3⟩ & =⟨4,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨-15,8,3⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-15,8,3⟩ & =-67\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-15,8,3⟩ & =-67 \\ -15x+8y+3z & =-67 \\ -15x+8y+3z+67 & =0 \\ 15x-8y-3z-67 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Given the Cartesian equation $5x+2y+z-4=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$

$(r-⟨0,0,$
{{field-1}}
$⟩)\cdot ⟨$
{{field-2}} $,\,2\,,$
{{field-3}}
$⟩=0$
content.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨5,2,1⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+2y+z-4 & =0 \\ z & =-5x-2y+4\end{aligned}
$$

If we put $x=0$ and $y=0$, we get $z=4.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,4)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,4⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,4⟩)\cdot ⟨5,\,2\,,1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
